coaching.subject: preflight failure conversion into a classified PassResult

metrics.claim_path: no-llm/no-network (structural; the fast claim check is a local HMAC verify)

findings.checklist_item: State whether the empty-projects fan-out fallback (list(read_projects().keys()) or [_query_project]) is covered by the preflight, and align the validated set with the set fetcher actually queries.
evidence: fetcher fan-out: project_list = list(read_projects().keys()) or [_query_project] (per 05b8 RCA)
incident green state is {legacy_default:'REB', projects:{}} — empty projects, single-project fallback path
plan validates keys()+legacy_default but not the empty-projects _query_project fallback
findings.finding: The validated set (read_projects().keys() PLUS legacy_default) may not match the set fan-out actually queries when projects is EMPTY. The fetcher uses list(read_projects().keys()) or [_query_project], falling back to the single configured JIRA_PROJECT when projects is empty — the exact green-state shape from the incident ({legacy_default:'REB', projects:{}}). The plan does not state whether the fallback project (_query_project / JIRA_PROJECT) is included in the preflight when projects is empty, so an invisible configured fallback could slip past.
findings.location: Approach — 'every project in read_projects(repo_root).keys() PLUS legacy_default (when set)'
scenarios: projects.json has empty projects and a legacy_default that is not the actual fan-out fallback key
the configured single-project fallback (JIRA_PROJECT) is itself decommissioned/invisible

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify GET /rest/api/3/project/search against Jira Cloud REST docs (path, query/pagination params, and that project keys appear at values[].key with isLast paging) and cite the doc/verification in the Approach, since this endpoint surface is used nowhere else in the repo and the tests only exercise a self-authored fake.
evidence: Plan quote: 'against the standard Jira Cloud "Get projects paginated" endpoint `GET /rest/api/3/project/search` (paginated via `startAt` with the response envelope's `values[].key` / `isLast`)'

search_files for 'project/search' returns zero hits in src/ — the endpoint is not exercised anywhere in the codebase; existing _direct_rest_get callers all hit /rest/api/3/issue/* or /rest/api/3/user/*

Testing section: every AC exercises a fake _direct_rest_get 'returns a project/search page' — the fake encodes the plan's own assumed envelope, so a real path/field/pagination mismatch (e.g. wrong param name, expand requirement, key vs id) would ship undetected

EVIDENCE CLASS: Partially-verified — the Jira Cloud vendor + transport is confirmed in-repo, but this specific endpoint surface (path, startAt/isLast pagination, values[].key) is Unverified against --help/docs
findings.finding: The preflight depends on the external Jira Cloud endpoint GET /rest/api/3/project/search plus its pagination model (startAt) and response envelope (values[].key, isLast), but this specific endpoint surface is used nowhere in the codebase today (only /rest/api/3/issue/* and /rest/api/3/user/* paths exist) and the plan verifies its path/pagination/field-shape only against a self-authored fake, not Jira docs or an existing call.
findings.location: Approach — 'the standard Jira Cloud "Get projects paginated" endpoint GET /rest/api/3/project/search ... values[].key / isLast'
scenarios: The real endpoint requires a different query/pagination param or returns keys under a different field than assumed → preflight silently sees an empty/partial visible set and either false-negatives (blocks a valid pass) or the pagination loop never terminates / stops early
isLast/startAt semantics differ from the assumed contract → preflight only sees the first page and marks legitimately-visible projects as invisible
findings.suggested_fix: Cite the Jira Cloud 'Get projects paginated' API doc URL confirming path, startAt/maxResults pagination, isLast, and values[].key; and add at least one test asserting the preflight issues the expected path/params and correctly follows pagination across a multi-page (isLast=false→true) response, so a real-contract mismatch is caught before ship.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify whether the preflight abort returns a classified PassResult (matching the existing _reconcile_exception_result contract) or propagates as an exception, and confirm the out-of-dir consumer _lib_ops.py run_pass_result path handles it.
evidence: Plan: 'FAIL FAST with a clear, actionable message' and 'Wire it at the reconcile pass entry (__main__.py run_pass_result, strictly before reconcile.reconcile_once)'
run_pass_result returns PassResult; existing reconcile_once exceptions are wrapped by _reconcile_exception_result (__main__.py:515-520) into a classified PassResult
_lib_ops.py:195 consumes result.disposition.canonical_exit / result.details, expecting a PassResult, not a raised exception
findings.finding: The plan wires a new preflight that 'raises'/'aborts' inside run_pass_result but does not state whether the preflight failure is converted into a classified PassResult (like the existing reconcile_once path via _reconcile_exception_result) or propagates as an uncaught exception; the out-of-dir consumer _lib_ops.py (run_pass_result at _lib_ops.py:195) and run_pass (__main__.py:431) both consume a returned PassResult and would crash on an uncaught raise.
findings.location: Approach / Sequencing — wiring at __main__.py run_pass_result (line 469); consumers _lib_ops.py:195 and __main__.py:431
scenarios: A library caller (_lib_ops.bridge run) triggers a preflight abort and receives an uncaught exception instead of a structured non-zero PassResult

findings.checklist_item: Specify the exact skip predicate at run_pass_result in terms of the available target_mode/route signals (e.g. skip when route=='preview' or target_mode.value=='dry-run'; note reconcile-check never reaches this call site).
evidence: run_pass_result only receives target_mode and route; no_write is set inside reconcile.py:744 (after preflight would run)
findings.finding: The read-only skip predicate is under-specified against the actual wiring at run_pass_result. The plan names 'dry-run / reconcile-check / preview' but does not map these to the concrete signals available before reconcile_once: reconcile-check is short-circuited earlier in main() and never reaches run_pass_result; preview arrives as route=='preview'; dry-run is identified only via target_mode.value=='dry-run'; and no_write is computed INSIDE reconcile_once (after the preflight point). Without stating which of target_mode/route the preflight inspects, the skip could either run against a read-only pass or fail to skip one.
findings.location: Approach / Sequencing — 'skipping read-only passes (dry-run / reconcile-check / preview)'; wiring at __main__.py run_pass_result
scenarios: A dry-run/preview pass triggers a live project/search probe against Jira, contradicting 'before any outbound mutation' intent
A live pass is mis-classified as read-only and skips the preflight
findings.suggested_fix: State that the preflight runs only when route not in {'preview'} and target_mode.value != 'dry-run', and note reconcile-check is already short-circuited upstream so no handling is needed there.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Either add a criterion that exercises the real /rest/api/3/project/search envelope (a recorded/contract fixture matching Jira Cloud's paginated response) or document why offline fixtures suffice for the transport boundary.
evidence: 'fake/injected transport (no live Jira): a fake client whose _direct_rest_get returns a project/search page'
E6(f): a proving command on a mock substitute that bypasses the new behavior does not prove the criterion
findings.finding: The preflight introduces a new live REST boundary (GET /rest/api/3/project/search), but every acceptance criterion is verified only against a fake/injected _direct_rest_get; no criterion exercises the real Cloud transport parsing/pagination end-to-end, and there is no documented rationale/deferral for the absence of a live check.
scenarios: The real project/search envelope shape (values[].key / isLast / nextPage semantics) differs from the fake fixture and the probe silently mis-parses against live Jira
findings.suggested_fix: Add a note that the fake fixture mirrors the documented Jira Cloud project/search envelope, and cite the endpoint contract, or defer a live smoke check to a named follow-up with rationale.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the retry-vs-fail-closed boundary (how many retries before transport-unavailable) and a pagination termination guard (handle absent/false isLast, empty values, and a max-page bound) for the project/search probe.
evidence: 'A hard auth/transport error ... fails closed with its own distinct "transport unavailable" message'
pagination 'via startAt with the response envelope's values[].key / isLast' — no termination guard against a missing isLast/empty page stated
findings.finding: The plan reuses the retry helper (_retry_sleep / JQL_RETRY_COUNT) but does not state how a transient/retryable error is distinguished from a hard fail-closed transport error, nor how the paginated project/search loop terminates safely (e.g. empty values, isLast never true, or a page cap).
scenarios: A transient 5xx exhausts retries — is that transport-unavailable or does it retry forever?
project/search returns a page with isLast absent or malformed and the loop never terminates
findings.suggested_fix: Specify: retry transient errors up to JQL_RETRY_COUNT then raise transport-unavailable; loop while not isLast and values non-empty, break on a defensive max-page cap, treating a malformed envelope as transport-unavailable.
